questions.q: Why is GDP not an adequate measure of the welfare of a country?
answer: Gross Domestic Product measures the total value of final goods and services produced in a country in a year, and it is a useful indicator of the size and growth of an economy. However, it is not an adequate measure of welfare, for several reasons.

answer.text: GDP tells us the total output but nothing about how it is shared. A rising GDP may go mainly to a few rich people while the majority remain poor, so higher GDP does not always mean better welfare for all.
GDP counts only what is bought and sold in the market. It leaves out valuable non-market work, such as household chores and services done within the family, and much of the informal economy.
GDP ignores harmful side effects like pollution and environmental damage that lower people's quality of life, and it may even count spending on defence or disasters as output.

answer: For these reasons, a rise in GDP does not necessarily mean a rise in true welfare.
